issue.title: Social smell identity match is currently done on slice instead of full dataset
issue.body:
@CorneJB 

> One of the challenges is that identity_match() happens on the slice level and this results in non-congruent identity_id's across slices. Using the mail-adresses and names in the slices introduces the noise that identity_match() normally solves. This could maybe be solved by applying identity_match() outside of the loop on the whole gitlog (probably incurring a performance hit) or using the start/end commit to define where it is applied.

Actually, the identity_match() should work on either, since the git log slice is in essence a git log table with fewer rows. In Kaiaulu 0.0.0.9000 it used to be applied only after a transform_* function, which led to the issue you noted for doing this inside a loop:


https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/2486a1a5d775e1338de20980266c67b52df23db3/vignettes/social_smells_showcase.Rmd#L222-L227

so I removed that requirement to be a network in 0.0.0.9500. Could you try applying it to the entire gitlog and mailing list as output from parse_gitlog and parse_mbox at the start of the following notebook as shown here but with also the mbox?

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/71dae8b29851453d58d85cdf331f42f79d9145e3/vignettes/gitlog_showcase.Rmd#L102-L114

In other words instead of inside the loop:

```r
  project_log <- list(project_git_slice=project_git_slice,project_mbox_slice=project_mbox_slice)
  project_log <- identity_match(project_log,
                                name_column = c("author_name_email","reply_from"),
                                assign_exact_identity,
                                use_name_only=TRUE,
                                label = "raw_name"
                                )
```

do:

```r
  project_log <- list(project_git=project_git,project_mbox=project_mbox)
  project_log <- identity_match(project_log,
                                name_column = c("author_name_email","reply_from"),
                                assign_exact_identity,
                                use_name_only=TRUE,
                                label = "raw_name"

  project_git <- project_log[["project_git"]]
  project_mbox <- project_log[["project_mbox"]]
```

outside the loop, and remove the associated step from inside the loops. I will update the Notebook once I have the chance. Thanks for catching this!

issue.body:
**Quoting @carlosparadis on #96**
> There is one more small thing I should point out, that may impact your analysis. Consider that, each slice of 3 months (or the slice of the time window you choose) subsets separately the git log and mailing list. It is unlikely on a large project, but it is possible one of the 4 cases occur:

>  * No gitlog data is found, if no file changes happened in 3 months
>  * No mailing list data is found, if no communication happened in 3 months
>  * Both gitlog and mailing list had activity
>  * Neither had activity

> In the code I wrote, which is similar to the one you are thinking of now, the slices were smaller, since I looked at them "per project issue", and these 4 case types appeared much more often. This in turn can make a smell to not being computed for certain slices, if it requires the gitlog, mailing list, or both. Whatever function we come up with to iterate and compute these, has to account for that.



**Quoting @CorneJB  on #96**
> It is very funny that you mention those 4 cases because one of those cases caused my first few hours struggle to get kaiaulu working. The first range I tried to analyze had no mailing list data, which results in some kind of non-descriptive `x is not a bipartite graph supply types' argument` error. Putting N/A in the table where it is applicable and writing some documentation that explains the probable cause would already clear it up a lot I think.

                                use_name_only=TRUE,

issue.title: Adding developer turnover metrics to smells notebook
issue.body:
Hi!

I made this today for analyzing the turnover between analysis windows based on the quality metrics in Magnoni (2016)'s dissertation. I did not really know where to put it in terms of branches, issues, and pulls, so I'm dropping it here to get some feedback and create a branch/pull if it is needed/wanted. The for-loop below uses  `project_git_slicestack`, which is a list containing the slices that are made during the social smells part of the social smells showcase vignette. 

```
## Initiate turnover variable
code_dev_turnover <- list()

## Loop through slices and calculate turnover based on Magnoni (2016)
for(i in 1:length(project_git_slicestack)){
  
  ## Calculate developer turnover between slices and add to smells table
  if(i != 1){
    
    x1 <- unique(project_git_slicestack[[i - 1]]$author_name_email)
    x2 <- unique(project_git_slicestack[[i]]$author_name_email)
  
    neldy <- length(setdiff(x1,x2))
    neby <- length(x1)
    neey <- length(x2)
  
    code_dev_turnover[i] <- signif((neldy / ((neby + neey)/2)), digits = 3)
    
    smells[[i]]$code_dev_turnover <- code_dev_turnover[i]
    
  } else { ## Don't calculate for the fist window and add to smells table
    
    code_dev_turnover[i] <- "NULL"
    
    smells[[i]]$code_dev_turnover <- code_dev_turnover[i]
    
  }
```

Kind regards,

Corné Broere

The purpose of this issue is to understand how can a dev-file network can be obtained at function granularity. The following links are cues to that. A more organized analysis is done in further comments. 

This file from Codeface employs ctags:

https://github.com/siemens/codeface/blob/e6640c931f76e82719982318a5cd6facf1f3df48/codeface/cluster/cluster.py#L1414

Exuberant Ctags basically is a parser that takes as input a source file (e.g. bla.py) and outputs metadata of functions and other data objects of said source code as another file. Making sense of the metadata file appears to be very confusing, see this question on SO:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41933837/understanding-the-ctags-file-format

However, Codeface relies on a python library to parse Ctags, making it much simpler. This implementation appears to be very efficient, as it seems to be just a wrapper to a C file that does the parsing (notice the github project hasn't be updated in a long while):

https://github.com/cloggo/python-ctags

Codeface also relies on this VCS python package, which appears to abstract implementations of version control systems (Git, Subversion):

https://github.com/codeinn/vcs

Lastly, I also found out Exuberant Ctags itself has been abandoned, and other project took over forking it since then: 

https://ctags.io/

Some functions also evolved: For example, parse_*_network() now has an alternative function parse_*_temporal_network(). Therefore parse_*_network() should be renamed to parse_*_bipartite_network() or renamed altogether. See #43.

issue.body: Created a pull request based on [issue 97](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/97). I might have messed up the name due to the offset of github issue numbers and the actual numbers in the text. The `identitiy_match()` function is now performed outside of the slicing loop, causing `identity_id's` to be congruent across slices. I have tested the notebook in this fashion and it appears to be performing as expected. Any feedback is more than welcome!
